### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**12** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via getItem (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getItem, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:name; the bare tail of client method meta.getItem, bound to GET /meta/:type/:name), meta.getItem (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:name, selected by route anchor /meta/:type/:name; the route ledger binds it to GET /meta/:type/:name))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/meta/:type/:name (route, 40 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **218** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **157** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **157**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **102** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c76c0e042ea1efc9ccb7b209a82dd8f0fc119953` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `20d74aa781a436870756ea70bfb1e492b957bd45` — the merge of head `03d20969e341ad9566aae4c738fefc6abee8b365` into base `c76c0e042ea1efc9ccb7b209a82dd8f0fc119953`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 20d74aa781a436870756ea70bfb1e492b957bd45 && git checkout 20d74aa781a436870756ea70bfb1e492b957bd45
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c76c0e042ea1efc9ccb7b209a82dd8f0fc119953 03d20969e341ad9566aae4c738fefc6abee8b365 && git checkout -B drift-repro c76c0e042ea1efc9ccb7b209a82dd8f0fc119953 && git merge --no-ff 03d20969e341ad9566aae4c738fefc6abee8b365

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c76c0e042ea1efc9ccb7b209a82dd8f0fc119953
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c76c0e042ea1efc9ccb7b209a82dd8f0fc119953` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `03d20969e341ad9566aae4c738fefc6abee8b365`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/app-bundle.zod.ts + packages/rest/src/meta-app-bundle-routes.ts (the route the docblock describes: `inObjectListOrder`, `inboundRelationObjects`, `appNavigationReach`, `addOnce`, the `objectList()` source), packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts `metaListSource` and packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-list-reads.ts (which list "the object list" is), packages/rest/src/meta-collection-routes.ts and packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts `createMetaListAnswer` (whether `GET /meta/object` reorders), content/docs/references/api/app-bundle.mdx (regenerated from the hits file), ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/app-bundle.ts and packages/client/src/index.ts `meta.getAppBundle` (the bundle's readers), packages/spec/src/api/app-bundle.test.ts (pins nothing on the sentences). Remainder of the diff (rest route and tests, route-ledger note, changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `AppMetadataBundleResponseSchema`: unchanged — right.** The hits file moves only the module docblock's `objects` bullet and the `objects` `.describe()` string. Keys, `z.array(GetMetaItemResponseSchema)`, `.strict()`, the two exported types and `lazySchema` wrapping are byte-identical to `main`. `packages/spec/src/api/app-bundle.test.ts` is untouched and still passes on the shape alone. No `exports` map change; no generated JSON schema on `main` carried the old sentence (searched the whole tree: only the zod file and the mdx did).
- **Public surface of `GET /meta/app/{appId}/bundle`: the ORDER of `objects` changes; the set does not — right, and declared.** At head the route serves `members('object', inObjectListOrder(listed, [...reach.objects, ...inbound]))` where `listed` is the same `objectList()` read that `inboundRelationObjects` already consumed. `inObjectListOrder` keeps every name once (`addOnce`), so the served set, and the `views`/`pages` derived from `served`, cannot move. The bytes change for every bundle whose reach-first derivation differs from list order; the spec now states the new order, so route and contract agree.
- **Which list "the object list" is — right.** The route reads `metaListSource(p, env).listMetaItems('object')`, which is `p.getMetaItemsForExecution`; `GET /meta/object` serves `p.getMetaItems`. Both bodies (`protocol-meta-list-reads.ts`) call `readFlattenedMetaItems(canonicalizeMetaRequestType(request), audience)` with the same request, differing only in serving decoration and redaction, so the enumeration order is one. `createMetaListAnswer` reorders only `view` lists under `?object=` (step 4); the object list is filtered per caller, never resorted. So the console's registry order (its `GET /meta/object`) and the bundle's order agree, which is what card #29680 asked for.
- **New export `inObjectListOrder` from `packages/rest/src/meta-app-bundle-routes.ts`: module-internal — not a published surface.** `packages/rest/src/index.ts` does not re-export the module (same posture as `appNavigationReach` and `inboundRelationObjects`).
- **Readers of `objects` order — the PR's claim checked and right.** `ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/app-bundle.ts` indexes members into `Map` by type then name; `packages/client` `meta.getAppBundle` passes the body through. Nothing read in the tree depends on reach-first position.
- **Prose nit for the lane seat (changeset and PR body, not a hits file):** "a bundle whose navigation already follows the object list is served byte for byte as before" is slightly over-broad. The exact unchanged class is "a bundle whose reach-first derivation already equals list order"; a navigation in list order whose inbound object sits EARLIER in the list than a navigation object still moves. The CONTROL test is a member of the exact class, so the test is right; only the sentence is loose.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/29680-app-bundle-object-list-order.md`: `@objectstack/rest` patch, `@objectstack/spec` patch. **Matches the diff.** `rest` is a behaviour fix on a served route with no API shape change (patch per AGENTS.md Post-Task 3); `spec` ships only docblock and `.describe()` text, which land in `dist` and in the generated reference, so a patch is owed and nothing above patch is.
- **`Clause-②: no` — right** (the PR body and the changeset both carry it, line-initial, no arm). The schema accepts exactly what it accepted on `main`; nothing widens or narrows. **`Metadata-protocol: none` — right**: no key an author writes is added, removed or re-meant.
- Gate verdicts on head `03d20969`: 62 check-runs at the third read — 24 `success`, 8 `skipped`, 30 still `in_progress`, **0 failures**. Completed green include `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Build Docs`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`. Still running: `Build Core`, `Test Core (1-8/8)`, `Test UI (1-16/16)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`. This record does not wait on them: the lane seat's ACCEPT and any auto-merge arm require the full set green (contract-review.md ②), and a red among them re-opens this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` in the os-dev-report — nothing to answer.
- Deviation 1 (the order's design-report path not on this project's mount; the card body's quoted measurement used instead): acceptable — the card body carries the measured before/after and the cause line, and this review reads the same.
- Deviation 2 (file surface widened to `app-bundle.zod.ts`, the regenerated mdx, `rest-route-ledger.ts`, a `@objectstack/spec` changeset): authorized by triage designation 6593258467 and recorded in claim amendment 6594006607; the PR's file list holds exactly those paths and nothing beyond.
- Deviation 3 (PR body template fold): prose, no contract effect.
- `check:dev-prereqs` exit 1 locally (unbuilt `ui/**` workspace): local state only; the derived families it would have covered are the in-progress CI runs named in ②.
- **Landing flag for the lane seat:** `content/docs/references/api/app-bundle.mdx` is a generated file, so `landing-operations.md` §D serial relay applies at landing, as triage and the claim amendment already noted. The PR is still a draft.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no outside-author note is owed.
- Escalations: none.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/app-bundle.zod.ts` judged against the ruling it implements (triage 6593258467: two order sentences stating the object-list order the fix serves, docs only) and against its first consumer, the route at head.

- **The docblock bullet against the route — holds, clause by clause.** (a) "every object an `object` navigation entry names (top-level `navigation`, each area's `navigation`, and `children` at any depth)" = `appNavigationReach` walking `a.navigation`, each `areas[].navigation`, and `e.children` recursively, taking `type === 'object'` entries' `objectName`. (b) "every object with a `lookup` or `master_detail` field whose `reference` is one of those" = `inboundRelationObjects` over `RELATIONSHIP_TYPES = {lookup, master_detail}` with `wanted.has(field.reference)`, against `reach.objects` only. (c) "all in the object list's order" = `inObjectListOrder`'s first loop over `listed`, which holds both the navigation names and the inbound names. (d) "a name the object list does not hold follows the listed ones, in navigation order" = the second loop over `names = [...reach.objects, ...inbound]`; every `inbound` name came from `listed`, so the only names reaching the tail are navigation names absent from the list, and they come out in `reach.objects` order. The clause is reachable (the by-name read resolves a legacy short name the list does not carry), so it is not dead text. (e) "One hop" = inbound judged against `reach.objects`, never against `inbound`. (f) The retained sentence "A name appears once per list, at its first position" = `addOnce` in both loops and in `appNavigationReach`. Tried to break it with: a duplicate name in `listed` (first position wins, matches "at its first position"); a navigation name absent from the list (tail, navigation order); an inbound object that is also a navigation object (the card's case: placed by list position, `contact` no longer rides reach-first); an empty navigation (empty `objects`, the sentence degenerate but true). No gap found.
- **The `.describe()` against the route — holds.** "The objects the app's navigation reaches and the objects whose relationship fields reference them, in the object list's order" states the set and the order the route serves. It omits the tail clause, which the docblock carries; a summary string omitting the edge is acceptable since the module docblock is the full contract and the generated page shows both.
- **The regenerated mdx against the hits file — byte-exact.** Extracted the `.describe()` string from the zod source (concatenated literal, escapes resolved) and compared it with the `objects` row of the generated table: identical. Normalized the docblock bullet and the mdx bullet: identical. The page still carries the AUTO-GENERATED banner. No other tracked artefact on `main` held the old sentence, so nothing else owed regeneration.
- **Against the scenario it is accepted against (card #29680 and #29552 leg 1):** the spec now promises the order the console's registry read serves, and the two orders are one enumeration (① third bullet). A console deriving related lists from the bundle's `objects` therefore sees the registry's order, which is the card's "Wanted".
- **should-fix (non-blocking):** the bullet says "the object list" without naming which list. A spec reader has no route to tie it to; the tree ties it to the protocol's object list, the one `GET /meta/object` serves (per-caller filtered, never reordered). One parenthetical such as "(the order `GET /meta/object` lists them in)" in the docblock bullet, regenerated into the mdx, would close that. Docs only, no shape change, can ride a later docs PR.
- **must-fix:** none.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-t365pj`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbXsK9j25sd7eVwW96G`

**VERDICT: PASS**
